title: lore agents --check: wrong-scope remedy for a local plugin override, exit 0 while the plugin-sourced SKILL.md is absent, and plain lore agents hides what it would write
description: Product bug, from opum-desktop measurement relayed by team-lead 2026-10-25, reproduced in this checkout (origin/dev 8291a945). Setup: opum-lore@opum enabled at user scope but overridden to false in the gitignored .claude/settings.local.json; .lore/config.toml has agents.skill_source = "plugin". (1) WRONG SCOPE: `lore agents --check` prints "plugin-claude disabled opum-lore@opum scope=user" and prescribes `claude plugin enable opum-lore@opum --scope user`; that cannot work because the local override wins, so the message names the wrong scope and points away from the file actually disabling the plugin. (2) EXIT CODE: the same run prints absent-plugin-sourced .claude/skills/lore/SKILL.md and exits 0 (opum-cli-e2e saw the same), so a missing skill is not caught. (3) A plain `lore agents` on an existing SKILL.md reports "protected" and writes nothing, so a reader cannot see what it would write without --force in a scratch copy (opum-desktop). Related: LCLI-129, LCLI-267, LCLI-271. Filed only; start nothing until the plan schedules it. Dependency on LCLI-764 is only so the repro stays live until that task changes this checkout, so record the repro output before then.

acceptanceCriteria.text: With the plugin enabled at user scope and overridden false in the checkout settings.local.json, the plugin-claude diagnostic names the scope or file that actually disables it, and its remedy is one that works

lore agents --check keeps an exit code that does not depend on plugin enablement; its output states plainly that up-to-date covers the managed block and the skill file only, and when skill_source is plugin, the plugin is disabled and no skill file is present, it says no lore skill is reachable in this checkout (DEC-238 a5; proved both ways, exit code identical in both states)
A reader can see what lore agents would write over a protected SKILL.md without --force on a scratch copy
A test pins each of the three behaviours and fails on a mutant that restores the old one

plan: 1. Measure the remedy in a scratch project (snapshot ~/.claude/settings.json and ~/.claude.json first)

2. Tests first with a fake plugin port + fixture settings files: local override names the file; no override names user; skill_source=plugin + disabled + no SKILL.md says no skill reachable; exit code identical across states
3. Implement detection from .claude/settings.local.json and .claude/settings.json in agent-plugins.ts; add the up-to-date coverage sentence
4. Scope criterion 3 (protected SKILL.md visibility) against existing flags; ask the leader if it needs a new one
5. Align remedy/coverage strings with quest-cli via team-lead; update cli-surface.md and CHANGELOG; mutation-test; bun test + bun run lore check
implementationNotes: The repro output for (1) and (2) is recorded verbatim in the LCLI-764 before-state note; that checkout stops reproducing once LCLI-764 lands, so use a scratch checkout with the same override afterwards. (The description sentence about a dependency on LCLI-764 is superseded: no dependency edge, it is not a prerequisite.)

DEC-238 (a5) 2026-10-25, RULED A (opum-doc#1356): criterion 2 amended, NO exit-code change. Reason: plugin enablement belongs to the machine (user scope plus gitignored settings.local.json), not the repository; a gate keyed to it would pass on one machine and fail on another, and lore exit codes are product surface for external users. Given up: automatic failure on a checkout sliding back into the LCLI-764 defect; the per-task criteria and a reader of the output are the control.

PROGRESS 2026-10-25 (criteria 1 and 2 built; 3 awaits a ruling, 4 stays open until 3 is built). Measured on Claude Code 2.1.309 in a scratch project with enabledPlugins false in its .claude/settings.local.json: plugin list --json gives ONE row scope user enabled false (effective, no deciding file); enable --scope user FAILS ("already enabled at user scope") and leaves it disabled; enable --scope local flips it to enabled and rewrites that file; ~/.claude/settings.json hash unchanged. Implementation: withClaudeSettingsOverride in src/core/agent-plugins.ts reads .claude/settings.local.json then .claude/settings.json for a disabled non-managed user/synced row, adds overriddenBy {scope,file}, a plugin-claude-override plain record and the --scope <local|project> remedy; agents.ts adds agents-coverage and agents-skill-reachability notes. Exit codes untouched. Tests (test/agent-plugins.test.ts, written before the fix, 6 red first): local/project override, controls (no file, enabling file, other plugin, bad JSON, installed, managed), plain record order, coverage, reachability both ways with identical exit codes, pretty view. Mutants: neutralising the override lookup (4 red), widening the reachability state (1 red), dropping the skill_source check (1 red). bun test 5333 pass 0 fail on rerun (one earlier full run had 1 unidentified fail; two later runs green). typecheck clean; lore check exit 0. OPEN: criterion 3 (see a protected SKILL.md pending write) needs a ruling A/B/C sent to team-lead; string alignment with quest-cli also pending.

DEC-238 a6 2026-10-25: remedy follows the scope where the override lives (local/project/user), JSON field renamed to override {scope,file} to match quest-cli PR 679, strings approved verbatim; criterion 3 built as RULED A: files[].pending on a protected SKILL.md (Claude and Codex) in JSON only, human output unchanged, no flag. Tests for pending written first; mutant dropping pending: 2 red. Full bun test 5338 pass 0 fail, typecheck clean, lore check 0. Quest-cli coordinated the bytes over messages (coverage word: lore says up-to-date; quest chooses its own verdict word, not ruled).

VERDICT: APPROVE. Opus post-merge security review of opum-ai/lore-cli#678 (LCLI-765), with 6 non-blocking findings.

SHA: 93943e000bb97e6d1352bedef0d73b2a98f64f70

SCOPE: The diff file (lore-cli-678.review.diff, 571 lines) was readable, and I read all of it. I treated .quest/completed/LCLI-765.json as the spec: criteria 1-4 plus the DEC-238 a5 and a6 notes. From the worktree I also read src/core/agent-plugins.ts lines 1-435 in full (remedyFor, checkFromListing, withClaudeSettingsOverride, updateLorePlugin, notRunReport), src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts (decodeClaudePluginList, CliAgentPluginPort, and bunPluginCommandRunner's Bun.spawn options), src/core/agent-bridge.ts (planSkill, buildSkillDoc), the head of buildCodexSkillDoc in src/core/codex-bridge.ts, runAgents and pluginChecks in src/commands/agents.ts, and how src/cli.ts:669-676 derives root. Read-only: I ran no tests and no mutants.

AUTHORING MODEL: argv --model claude-sonnet-5-5; 237/237 assistant turns on claude-sonnet-5-5, none on DeepSeek (leader-measured from transcript 46084853-c846-4b59-b1b9-3093d3198dbb). Implementation met DEC-182 (2)'s Sonnet floor; the gap was the missing Opus review only.

ANSWERS TO THE SECURITY QUESTIONS
- Reading settings: disablesPlugin (src/core/agent-plugins.ts:310-318) runs readFileSync(join(root, <constant>)). The only two paths are the literals .claude/settings.local.json and .claude/settings.json (lines 304-307), so no input from data can steer the path. The parse is wrapped in try/catch and any failure means "no override". The only thing taken from the file is one boolean, enabledPlugins["opum-lore@opum"] === false. A __proto__ key from JSON.parse becomes an own property, so there is no prototype pollution. An array, null or non-object value for enabledPlugins also means "no".
- Injection: the remedy at :341 is built only from the constant LORE_PLUGIN_ID and override.scope, which comes from the constant table. The printed file comes from the same table. No settings-file bytes reach any output.
- Escalation: none. A managed row and an unnamable scope both return at :337 before any override logic, and only a disabled user or synced row is rewritten (:338). The remedy only ever narrows, from user to local or project. With no override the old --scope user remedy is unchanged.
- Writes: none. The new code only reads settings. The one mutation path is still port.update, which runs claude plugin update and is reached only for an installed, non-managed row (:419). An override only applies to a disabled row, so the two never meet, and nothing runs claude plugin enable.
- files[].pending: it is set only on a protected plan (agent-bridge.ts:470, codex-bridge.ts:351) and always equals desired, which is buildSkillDoc() or buildCodexSkillDoc(). Both are constant strings built in code with no repository or on-disk input. The protected file's own bytes are never put in pending, so nothing from outside the repository and no secrets can leak. --plain and pretty print only the path and the action, and test/agents.test.ts pins both.
- Managed remedy first: confirmed by remedyFor (:261) and the :337 early return, and pinned by "an override file does not rewrite an INSTALLED plugin's report, and a managed row still decides first".
- Exit codes: coverageNotes only adds output lines. Tests assert identical codes across the disabled, enabled and not-installed states.

FINDINGS (all non-blocking)
1. A special file behind a symlink can hang or exhaust lore (src/core/agent-plugins.ts:312, non-blocking hardening). readFileSync follows symlinks and has no isFile or size cap. If a checkout commits .claude/settings.json as a symlink to a FIFO, open blocks forever and lore agents --check or lore init hangs with no timeout. A symlink to /dev/zero reads until memory or a length limit runs out. The try/catch catches neither in time. It only fires when the Claude row is disabled at user or synced scope, and at most one boolean is derived, so nothing leaks. Suggested fix: lstat or stat, require isFile, and cap the size (settings files are KB).
2. The precedence walk is "first file that sets false", not "first file that sets the key" (:326). If local sets true and project sets false, the walk skips local and names project. Claude itself would report that state as enabled, so a disabled row should not reach it, and in normal use this is latent. The "local beats project" test only covers both files set to false. A stricter walk would stop at the first file whose value is a boolean.
3. root is the process cwd, not the repository root (src/cli.ts:671 for agents; init is the same at :429). Bun.spawn (src/adapters/agent-plugins.ts:102) passes no cwd, so the listing and the file read agree on the directory, which is good. But a run from a subdirectory reads <subdir>/.claude/settings*.json. If the override sits at the repository root, it is not found and the report falls back to the old --scope user remedy, which is the LCLI-765 defect again. That degrades and never escalates. Whether Claude Code itself walks up to find .claude/ is not established here (see UNVERIFIED).
4. Test gaps; mutants I would expect to survive:
   (a) The test titled "controls: repo source, an unreadable listing, or a present skill file never claim unreachability" (test/agent-plugins.test.ts, LCLI-765 block) never builds the present-skill-file case. A mutant that drops the skillAbsent condition from coverageNotes (src/commands/agents.ts) should stay green.
   (b) No test has a synced row, so dropping `synced` from :338 survives.
   (c) No test has a disabled local- or project-scope install row with an override file, which should stay unchanged, so widening :338 survives.
   (d) init.ts:1039 and :1462 gained options.root, but no init test uses an override file, so reverting either call survives.
   The agents path does pin the main behaviours both ways: override and no override, the four parse controls, the plain record order, reachability true and false with equal exit codes, and pending present and absent for Claude and Codex.
5. The --scope project remedy rewrites a committed file. It matches DEC-238 a6 ("remedy follows the scope where the override lives"), so it is not a defect. But running it flips enablement for every collaborator, whereas --scope local would override project for this machine only. This is for opum-doc to weigh if it wants to. I am not proposing a change.
6. Docs and CHANGELOG match the code. CHANGELOG and cli-surface.md describe reachability as "disabled or missing" (not-installed included), which is wider than criterion 2's "disabled". That is a reasonable superset and is tested. The mid-task rename left no stale overriddenBy anywhere in src/, test/ or docs/. No JSON schema file contains "remedy", so no closed schema needs override or pending added.

UNVERIFIED
- Nothing in the record measures that claude plugin enable opum-lore@opum --scope project actually flips a user-installed plugin disabled by .claude/settings.json. The record and cli-surface.md measure only --scope local, on Claude Code 2.1.309. Nothing measures synced rows either.
- Whether Claude Code reads .claude/settings*.json from cwd only or walks up to the repository root. This decides how much finding 3 matters.
- The test results (5338 pass), typecheck and lore check exit 0, and the mutant counts in the record are the writer's. I had no shell to re-run them.
- How Bun's readFileSync behaves on /dev/zero (throws at a length limit versus OOM) is inferred, not run.
finalSummary: lore agents --check now names the checkout settings file that disables opum-lore (override {scope,file}, plugin-claude-override record, remedy --scope local or project, measured to work where --scope user fails), states that up-to-date covers the managed block and skill file only, says when no lore skill is reachable, and a protected SKILL.md carries pending bytes in --json (DEC-238 a5/a6). Exit codes unchanged. Verified with tests written first, mutants, bun test 5338 pass 0 fail, typecheck, lore check.
